title: India AI Funding Nearly Doubles to $1.6B in 9M 2026, As Early-Stage Funding Nearly Triples
summary: India AI funding nearly doubled to 1.6 billion dollars in the first nine months of 2026

sentences: Tracxn Technologies Limited, a leading data intelligence platform, released the India AI – 9M 2026 Report, covering funding, investors, exits, unicorns and city-level activity across India’s AI ecosystem from Jan 1, 2026 to Sep 30, 2026.
India AI companies raised $1.6B in equity funding in 9M 2026, up 96% from $822M in 9M 2025 and 162% from $616M in 9M 2024, marking the highest funding total across the 9M periods covered since 2019.
The funding was raised across 87 rounds, down 42% from 149 in 9M 2025, indicating that the increase was driven by a relatively small number of large deals.
Early Stage funding led the investment mix, while Mumbai overtook Bengaluru to become the largest funding city during the period.
The ten largest rounds of 9M 2026 raised $1.5B, or 90% of the $1.6B total.
Neysa, a Mumbai-based AI cloud provider, raised the largest, a $600M Series B in Feb, equal to 37% of all funding and 76% of the $791M increase over 9M 2025.
Sarvam, a Bengaluru-based generative AI developer, raised $255M in a Series B in Jun and a further $90.4M in Aug.
Yotta raised $150M in a Series D in Jul.
Series A and later rounds fell 33% to 24 from 36, and first-time funded companies fell 60% to 24 from 60.
Worldwide, AI companies raised $383.5B in 9M 2026.
India’s $1.6B was 0.4% of that, ninth among countries.
Early Stage funding rose 191% to $1.3B in 9M 2026 from $434M in 9M 2025, and its share of all funding grew to 78% from 53%.
Early Stage rounds fell 38% to 21, and the average Early Stage round was $60.2M, against $12.8M.
Late Stage funding rose 4% to $280M across 3 rounds, 17% of the total.
Seed funding fell 42% to $69.2M, 4% of the total, and Seed rounds fell 44% to 63 from 113.
On the investor side, 111 investors backed India AI companies in 9M 2026, down 34% from 169.
First-time investors fell 39% to 43, and international investors fell 38% to 29.
Peak XV Partners led Early Stage investors with 3 investments, followed by Prosus and Khosla Ventures with 2 each.
Antler, IvyCap Ventures and Finvolve each made 2 Seed investments, and SoftBank Vision Fund and Creaegis each backed 1 Late Stage round.
Mumbai’s share of India AI funding rose to 48% in 9M 2026 from 2% in 9M 2025, with $765M raised, against $15.7M.
Neysa and Yotta were its largest rounds.
Bengaluru raised $711M, a 44% share, against 54% a year earlier, led by Sarvam and Emergent.
Chennai was third with $75.5M, 5% of the total, most of it from Freehand’s $75M Series B.
The three cities together took 96% of all funding.
Ranked by segment, Enterprise Applications companies raised $1.6B, against $780M in 9M 2025.
Enterprise Infrastructure companies raised $362M, against $166M, and Semiconductors companies raised $32.8M, against $16.8M.
India AI produced 3 new unicorns, companies valued at $1B or more, in 9M 2026, against 1 in 9M 2025: Neysa in Feb, Sarvam in Jun and Emergent in Jul.
Worldwide, 70 AI companies became unicorns, and India’s 3 were about 4% of them.
On exits, India AI companies recorded 6 acquisitions, against 5 in 9M 2025 and 2 in 9M 2024.
ExactSpace was acquired by Thermax for $3.4M in Feb, the only deal with a disclosed price.
C2I Semiconductors was acquired by Infineon for an undisclosed sum in Aug.
WeCP was acquired by Invisible Tech for an undisclosed sum in Mar.
Rampp.ai was acquired by Fastenal for an undisclosed sum in Jun.
No acquirer completed more than one deal.
No public listings were recorded, the same as in 9M 2025 and 9M 2024.
Worldwide, AI companies recorded 175 acquisitions and 26 public listings.
